newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament adjourns after MPs' brawl.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament adjourns after MPs' brawl.

text.p: Turkish parliament speaker on Tuesday had to adjourn a crucial debate over a censure motion against the Islamist-led government following a brawl by the deputies.
"I call a 10 minute break," speaker Mustafa Kalemli told the house during the session broadcast live on television.

MPs began to rush to the front after main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz referred to a statement by the army that accused the government of hostility towards Kemal Ataturk, secularist Turkey's revered founder.
"The general staff said 'We cannot be in harmony with the enemies of Ataturk'," Yilmaz said.
Parliament was discussing a censure motion submitted against Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his cabinet over the government's Islamist leanings.
Parliamentary deputies shoved and kicked each other, while one deputy was squeezed to shoulder height and literally carried off in a tide of other MPs to the side of the house.
Private NTV television said parliamentary bodyguards had been appointed to protect Yilmaz following the shoving match.
